--- title: "Model 2 — Random Forest" subtitle: "Bagged trees via ranger — a robust, low-tuning baseline" --- > **Where we are:** Second of six model documents in the > [House Prices — Tidymodels Tour](../index.qmd). Same structure as > [XGBoost](02-xgboost.qmd): recipe → spec → workflow → tune → finalize → > evaluate → save. We model `log(SalePrice)` and score on RMSE. ## Why a random forest? Where boosting builds trees sequentially to correct residuals, a random forest *bags* hundreds of decorrelated deep trees and averages them. It is famously hard to overfit, needs almost no tuning (really just `mtry`), and gives a strong baseline plus a permutation-importance read on which features matter. ## Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R")) source(here("R", "02_features.R")) library(tidyverse) library(tidymodels) library(here) library(vip) library(ranger) # the engine ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} train <- readr::read_csv(here("data", "processed", "train.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(SalePrice = log(SalePrice)) ``` ::: ## Recipe, spec, workflow ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rf_recipe <- make_recipe(train) # 1000 trees fixed (more is just slower, not better once stable); tune mtry and # min_n. importance = "permutation" so we can plot variable importance. rf_spec <- rand_forest( mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 1000 ) |> set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |> set_mode("regression") rf_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rf_recipe) |> add_model(rf_spec) ``` ::: ## Tuning with 10-fold cross-validation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(42) folds <- vfold_cv(train, v = 10, strata = SalePrice) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # mtry's upper bound depends on the number of predictors, so finalize against # the baked training data. preds <- prep(make_recipe(train, num_comp = 2)) |> bake(new_data = NULL) |> select(-SalePrice, -Id) rf_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_wf) |> finalize(preds) |> update(num_comp = num_comp(range = c(2L, 15L))) set.seed(42) rf_grid <- grid_space_filling(rf_params, size = 20) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rf_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, rsq) set.seed(42) rf_tuned <- tune_grid( rf_wf, resamples = folds, grid = rf_grid, metrics = rf_metrics, control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = TRUE) ) saveRDS(rf_tuned, here("models", "rf_res.rds")) ``` ::: ### Tuning results ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} autoplot(rf_tuned, metric = "rmse") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![RMSE across the tuning grid (autoplot).](03-random-forest_files/figure-html/tune-plot-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_best(rf_tuned, metric = "rmse", n = 5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Finalize and fit ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} best_rf <- select_best(rf_tuned, metric = "rmse") best_rf ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} final_rf_wf <- finalize_workflow(rf_wf, best_rf) set.seed(42) rf_fit <- fit(final_rf_wf, data = train) ``` ::: ## Cross-validated performance ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} collect_metrics(rf_tuned) |> semi_join(best_rf, by = names(best_rf)) |> select(.metric, mean, std_err, n) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ### Observed vs predicted (out-of-fold) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} collect_predictions(rf_tuned) |> filter(.config == best_rf$.config) |> ggplot(aes(x = SalePrice, y = .pred)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) + geom_point(alpha = 0.35, colour = house_pal[1]) + labs(title = "Random Forest — CV predicted vs observed", x = "Observed log(SalePrice)", y = "Predicted log(SalePrice)") + coord_equal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Out-of-fold predicted vs observed log(SalePrice).](03-random-forest_files/figure-html/obs-pred-1.png){width=528} ::: ::: ### Variable importance ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rf_fit |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> vip(num_features = 15, geom = "col", aesthetics = list(fill = house_pal[2])) + labs(title = "Random forest variable importance") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Top features by permutation importance.](03-random-forest_files/figure-html/vip-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Save the fitted workflow ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} saveRDS(rf_fit, file = here("models", "rf_fit.rds")) ``` ::: ## Submission ```bash quarto render docs/submission.qmd -P model:rf ``` ## Next steps - Continue to the **[Neural Net](04-neural-net.qmd)**, which leans on the normalized/PCA recipe. - Back to the **[master results table](../index.qmd)**.
